newsitem.title: GERMANY: Linotype shareholders accept takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: Linotype shareholders accept takeover bid.

text.p: Germany's Linotype Hell AG said on Monday more than 25 percent of its shares were offered to Heidelberger Druckmaschinen AG in the open market under a takeover bid which ran from July 25 to September 13.

The shares were offered to Commerzbank AG which will pass them on to Heidelberger Druck -- along with a stake of 50 percent plus one share previously owned by Siemens AG and Frega Vermoegen verwaltungsgesellschaft mbH -- once the Federal Cartel Office has approved the takeover.

The shareholders' acceptance of Heidelberger Druck's offer enables the Heidelberg-based printing machinery group to buy at least 75 percent plus one share in Linotype Hell AG, a leading manufacturer of high-resolution laser image setters and electronic colour systems.
Heidelberger Druck is a subsidiary of Rheinelektra, a holding company whose own business is principally engaged in the supply of electricity.
Linotype has said the bid will secure its financial future as cooperation between the two firms will open up considerable synergies and opportunities for cost-cutting.
Heidelberger Druck offered 95 marks per share. Linotype's shares closed at 95 marks on Friday.
